import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Drop 'Person ID' as it's not needed for analysis
df = df.drop(columns=['Person ID'])

# Set a clean style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep,
# differentiated by BMI Category and showing Stress Level as point size.
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='BMI Category',
    size='Stress Level',
    sizes=(50, 500),  # Adjust point size range
    alpha=0.7,        # Set transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    palette='viridis', # Choose a color palette
    legend='full'     # Ensure all legend elements are shown
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep by BMI Category and Stress Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
# For both hue and size legends
handles, labels = scatter_plot.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Filter out duplicate labels for 'Stress Level' if they appear
unique_labels = {}
for i, label in enumerate(labels):
    if label not in unique_labels:
        unique_labels[label] = handles[i]

# Create new handles and labels list based on unique_labels order
new_handles = list(unique_labels.values())
new_labels = list(unique_labels.keys())

# Place the combined legend outside the plot area
plt.legend(new_handles, new_labels, title='Legend', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
